messages.text: PSG's Kvaratskhelia set for surgery after ACL rupture in win over Barca

metadata.summary: Paris Saint-Germain winger Kvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to have surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), the French club have confirmed.
metadata.content: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia: PSG forward set for surgery after rupturing ACL in Champions League win over Barcelona | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Breaking Khvicha Kvaratskhelia: PSG forward set for surgery after rupturing ACL in Champions League win over Barcelona Wednesday 21 October 2026 11:03, UK Image: PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sustained a serious knee injury in the Champions League win over Barcelona Paris Saint-Germain winger Kvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to have surgery after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), the French club have confirmed. The 25-year-old, who was named the Champions League's best player last season, was injured in Tuesday's 4-2 home win over Barcelona. The European champions have said Kvaratskhelia will have an operation "in the coming days" but gave no timeline for his recovery. Report: PSG 4-2 Barcelona Champions League fixtures and results PSG's fixtures The injury raises serious concerns over whether Kvaratskhelia will play again this season, but he will definitely miss PSG's Champions League trip to Aston Villa on December 8. Kvaratskhelia has been nominated for the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a stellar campaign last season as he helped PSG earn back-to-back Champions League titles as well as Ligue 1 glory. PSG also lost Ousmane Dembele , the reigning Ballon d'Or holder, and captain Marquinhos to injury against Barca. metadata.summary: Christian Horner has revealed he helped Mercedes sign Lewis Hamilton after holding early discussions with the British driver's management to join Red Bull.
metadata.content: Christian Horner reveals Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton management before telling Mercedes' Niki Lauda to sign British driver | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Christian Horner reveals Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton management before telling Mercedes' Niki Lauda to sign British driver Christian Horner joins Simon Lazenby on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show Podcast to reveal all on Red Bull talks with Lewis Hamilton before the latter joined Mercedes and his thoughts on Kimi Antonelli, who could become world champion this Sunday at the United States GP Wednesday 21 October 2026 09:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains how he convinced Niki Lauda to sign Hamilton for Mercedes in 2012. Christian Horner has revealed he helped Mercedes sign Lewis Hamilton after holding early discussions with the British driver's management to join Red Bull. Hamilton left McLaren to join Mercedes at the start of 2013 but in Horner's new book, 'Drive ', which will be on sale from this Thursday, he says Hamilton showed interest to join Red Bull. Senior figures at Red Bull, including co-owner Dietrich Mateschitz, were not keen on the move that would have seen Hamilton replace Mark Webber and become Sebastian Vettel's team-mate from 2013. messages.text: NBA season tips off as Detroit stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Celtics

metadata.summary: Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win.
metadata.content: NBA: Detroit Pistons stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Boston Celtics as season tips off in style | NBA News | Sky Sports Skip to main content NBA: Detroit Pistons stage epic 22-point comeback to defeat Boston Celtics as season tips off in style Detroit Pistons rally from 22-points down to beat Boston Celtics 121-113 with Javonte Green and Cade Cunningham’s 22 points and 8 assists winning the day at Little Caesars Arena Tuesday 20 October 2026 23:19, UK Image: Detroit Pistons guard Cade Cunningham (2) drives on Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum (0) in the NBA season tip off Detriot Pistons staged an epic 23-0 run in the fourth quarter as they overcame a 22-point deficit - the largest come-from-behind win against the Boston Celtics in the last 30 seasons - to seal a stunning 121-113 win. Javonte Green scored 19 points after not playing in the first half and Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points and eight assists, helping the Pistons to victory as the NBA season tipped off in style on Tuesday. Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown. messages.text: Have set-piece kings Arsenal really become set-piece strugglers?

metadata.summary: Arsenal scored a Premier League-high 25 non-penalty set-piece goals on their way to winning the title last season. But have 'Set-piece FC' lost their not-so-secret edge?
metadata.content: Arsenal were set-piece kings last season, so why have they stopped scoring from set-pieces? Between the Lines explains | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Arsenal were set-piece kings last season, so why have they stopped scoring from set-pieces? Between the Lines explains Arsenal are yet to score from a set-piece this season, excluding penalties, so what's happened? Between the Lines digs into the numbers, reveals their open-play improvement, and explains why the set-piece goals may start to flow again soon By Nick Wright, Adam Smith and David Fraser Wednesday 21 October 2026 08:45, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Have Arsenal gone from set-piece kings to set-piece strugglers? Sky Sports takes a look in Between the Lines. Arsenal scored a Premier League-high 25 non-penalty set-piece goals on their way to winning the title last season. But have 'Set-piece FC' lost their not-so-secret edge? Seven games into the new campaign, the Gunners are one of only four sides, along with Liverpool, Manchester United and Nottingham Forest, yet to score a non-penalty set-piece goal. Arsenal's total last season included a record 19 from corners and made it five straight Premier League seasons in which they have scored at least 15 non-penalty set-piece goals.
